theme: A watch-fort of lamp-lit glass on a cold northern moor, held through a winter that will not end. Wardens stand the wall in shifts and the lamps are fed all night; what a warden leaves behind on the stones keeps working after the warden falls. Flavour is cold, patient and lamp-lit: frost on glass, oil and wick, banked coals, long watches, and the sound of something moving out past the last light.

mechanics.name: Vigil
mechanics.description: A warden keeps its post. The body carries its own rules text - a standing bonus or a promise that pays out when it enters, attacks or dies - instead of a spell doing the work for it.

mechanics.name: Emberwork
mechanics.description: Lamp-glass is spent, never hoarded. A permanent pays itself away, or taps its own heat, for a burst of fire.

mechanics.name: Deepwatch
mechanics.description: The night shift reads the dark, thins what is coming and keeps its own hand full.

archetypeNotes: WG wants wardens that are worth the mana on the turn they land and still worth it three turns later.
UB wants card flow and a mill clock as an alternate finish.
WR wants cheap bodies that convert into damage before the wall gives.
